test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 28 June, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: Which form of government is established by the Constitution of India both, at the centre and states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Parliamentary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Indian Constitution** institutes a** parliamentary system** of governance at **both the central and state levels,** presenting a federal structure with certain unitary characteristics.
 
• It draws its foundation from the Westminster model, entrusting control over finances to elected representatives in adherence to the principle of **"no taxation without representation."**
 
• Within a federal framework, authority is divided between the central and state governments, a delineation clearly outlined in the Indian Constitution concerning legislative powers.
 
• The Constitution proclaims India as a sovereign democratic republic, encompassing an autonomous judiciary, safeguarded fundamental rights, and directive principles of state policy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Council of Ministers,** led by the **Chief Minister, **advises the Governor in Indian governance and administration at the central, state, and local levels.
 
• This section offers insights into the Constitution of India, the functioning of Parliament and Legislature, Union administration, as well as state, district, and local administration.
